reviews.classification: Historical performance audit with later implementations and explicitly limited integration evidence
reviews.disposition: Preserved original measurements and chronology; folded later cache, visibility, storage and nonce qualifications into the audit owner. F2 and unexercised audit-remainder browser coverage remain open rather than inferred from finite fuzz success.
reviews.evidence: Fresh full read of all 691 pre-fold lines in sequential bounded chunks; original probes, later fixes, integration-branch reports, failed budgets and final F1 correction compared within the document. No present runtime rerun or performance claim.

folds.heading: ## Content reconciliation B392: later corrections and remaining performance proof limits
folds.body:
This chronological audit preserves its original probes, later fixes and failed or contaminated measurements. Its Oct. 14 Chrome, CPU, renderer, launch, build and test counts describe those fixtures and host conditions. A fresh browser context provides storage isolation; a distinct port provides server separation. Neither renderer count nor a single busy-host run establishes steady-state cost. The leaked-server shell example demonstrates a subshell PID ownership failure, not permission to terminate current processes by port. Current test routing follows AD36 and the machine-wide npm test limiter, without wrapping it in another limiter.

The initial retired-key, hidden-preview and publication-frame changes have bounded fresh and developed-fixture evidence. Inclusive fact-building and preview percentages overlap and must not be added. The later AF1 and AF2 sections supersede the early provisional Map and duplicate-cache proposals: one read-frame owner, nested-frame restoration and invalidation at mutation boundaries matter more than preserving the original implementation. D1 cache identity includes the relevant state, sequence, clock, registry, actor, target and context fields; a context object identity alone is insufficient. Selected deterministic comparisons, focused tests and the historical browser routes do not establish every module or present-day performance.

The long-session seed eventually exhausted its available actions, so flat storage during further idle stepping does not bound every growth path. The 4 MiB backup allowance and catalogue-bound log explanations are hypotheses; an absent search result does not establish an unbounded population. The old reload and away-ledger observations precede later clock and away-bank work. Recheck their current owners before treating them as open runtime defects or treating saved_at as permanently nonsemantic. D3 reduced counter-only paused writes, but normal calendar, XP and due-state changes still wrote each tick. Its near-zero playing benefit and failed KB/min budget remain in the record; a quieter host producing more ticks is not a bytes-per-write regression.

D4 used an emulated document visibility state in headless Chrome, not an actual background-tab scheduling guarantee. The hidden refresh queue coalesces presentation while retaining gameplay-sensitive customization, polling, clocks, saves and other required work. Its two wall-time ratios were approximately 0.27 and 0.17, so the stated 0.20 target was met in one repetition. Reveal and save comparisons cover the recorded fixture. Worker use alone does not prove immunity to browser throttling.

RT8 fastForward counts engine ticks, whose game-time duration can differ during sleep. It pauses the engine across yields, preserves the open stepper batch, coalesces final rendering and saving, and does not grant player offline time. Its approximately 30 ms slicing cannot divide one expensive tick. The within-plan progress_time boundary drain remained a separate synchronous-path proposal. Preserve the historical long-task noise and storage-budget failures alongside the successful selected identity and responsiveness checks.

The final F1 section supersedes the earlier open sequence-chunking finding: one nonce increment per played minute, including audit-remainder entry, repaired the reproduced split-versus-jump mismatch. The finite fuzz corpus, unchanged selected one-minute hashes and historical rebuilt routes support that fix. They do not close F2's unbounded-advance soft-brick concern, prove a browser fixture with an audit remainder open, or establish present master integration. The wave merge was into its named integration branch under its recorded authorization, not evidence of a master merge. Old desktop widths, universal full-suite prompts, inactive milestone gates and process identifiers remain history under current PROJECT, AD36, AD39 and AD42 direction.

scope: Reviewer supplied content dispositions. Explicit read_mode distinguishes fresh reading from inspected prior full-content review reused on unchanged inputs. No hash-inferred semantics or renewed historical behavior proof.
